subject.title: [Bug]: google-shared payload converter strips layout dimensions from user-provided base64 images

question: Should OpenClaw define canonical per-image sizing/media-resolution metadata for ImageContent, or should width/height remain unsupported input shape outside the Google converter contract?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses the core ImageContent API, gateway input normalization, media preprocessing, and Google provider mapping; code inspection shows no existing width/height contract to repair mechanically.

options.title: Define canonical sizing contract
options.body: Add a deliberate ImageContent/media preprocessing contract and map supported Google behavior through mediaResolution or actual resizing, with tests for affected providers.

options.title: Use existing compression policy
options.body: Treat model mediaInput and image compression as the supported way to control image size/token cost, and document that per-image width/height metadata is not accepted.

options.title: Close as unsupported shape
options.body: Close this report if maintainers do not want a new image metadata contract and require reporters to provide a supported input path instead.

recommendation.title: Define canonical sizing contract
recommendation.body: Add a deliberate ImageContent/media preprocessing contract and map supported Google behavior through mediaResolution or actual resizing, with tests for affected providers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the only clear current-main history owner for the relevant converter and ImageContent contract.
